goal: Catch a commit made without proving the change works, at the moment it happens: log it in observe, stop it in enforce (agent-kit R32, run 2026-11-27-r32-hook-gates, unit 3).
changed: bstack ships a Claude Code PreToolUse hook on Bash, hooks/commit_gate.py. A git commit (with -C, -c, env prefixes or after && included; commit-tree not) in a session that ran no verify-work, verify-<app> skill, interrogate, code-review, review subagent or second opinion since its last commit that went through is judged.

The mode comes from policy.checks.commit-gate in ~/.agents/policy.yaml and the repo's .agents/policy.yaml, the stricter of the two, observe when neither names it. Observe logs a would-block lesson to the weekly flags run and allows. Enforce denies twice per commit, then lets the next through and logs why. Off does nothing. Any error allows and prints one line.
hooks/checks.py holds the mode reader, the per-session state and the flags-run logger, for the Stop hook to share. bstack 0.52.0.

claims.claim: Run as Claude Code runs it, the hook logs and allows in observe, denies twice then lets through with the reason in enforce, does nothing in off, counts each kind of verification and no other, restarts its count after a commit lands, judges only git commit, takes the stricter of the two policy files, and fails open on a broken event.
